con1-canon4-en: Was Maximus the Cynic never a true bishop, and are all ordinations and acts done by or concerning him invalid?
con1-canon5-en: Are those in Antioch who confess the unity of the Godhead of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost to be received in regard to the Western bishops' tome?
con1-canon6-en: Must accusations against orthodox bishops who administer the Churches be examined carefully, so that neither every person may accuse freely nor all accusers be shut out?
con1-canon7-en: Are Arians, Macedonians, Sabbatians, Novatians, Quarto-decimans, and Apollinarians who turn to orthodoxy received after written renunciation, anathematizing heresy, and sealing with holy oil?
con1-creed-en: Do we believe in one God the Father Almighty, and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son, Light of Light, of one substance with the Father, who became man, was crucified, rose, and ascended, and in the Holy Ghost the Lord and Giver of life?
con1-synodal-letter-en: Did the bishops assembled at Constantinople thank God for establishing the emperor's empire for the common peace of the Churches and report the synod's acts for the support of the true Faith?
con1-canons-preamble-en: Have the bishops assembled by God's grace in Constantinople on Emperor Theodosius's summons decreed canons for the Church?
lyo1-colli-constitution1-en: Does the general clause "certain others" in papal letters bring no more than three or four persons to court, whose names the petitioner must state in the first citation?
lyo1-collii-constitution1-en: Must bishops, abbots, and other administrators follow rules protecting churches from ruinous debt and usury, rather than excuse inefficient administration by blaming predecessors?
lyo1-colli-constitution2-en: May the apostolic see or its legates entrust cases only to persons of dignity or of high collegiate churches, and only in cities or well-known places with learned lawyers?
lyo1-collii-constitution2-en: Is the liberation of the empire of Constantinople among the constant pastoral cares for which the apostolic see seeks remedy and Catholic aid?
lyo1-colli-constitution3-en: Must someone bringing several personal claims against another obtain letters to the same judges on all claims, or else lose validity and pay the defendant's expenses?
lyo1-collii-constitution3-en: Should prelates admonish the people in their charge to seek God's favor for the recovery of the holy Land, for which the Church's children have long spent money and blood?
lyo1-colli-constitution4-en: If someone challenges an election, postulation, or provision and appeals to the apostolic see, must objector and defendant come within a month, after which the case may proceed despite absence?
lyo1-collii-constitution4-en: Does the Church mourn and seek to resist the Tartars' devastation of Christian countries such as Poland, Russia, and Hungary, aimed at destroying the Christian religion?
lyo1-colli-constitution5-en: Are conditional, alternative, and indefinite votes in elections, postulations, and ballots invalid, so that election is determined only by unconditional votes?
lyo1-collii-constitution5-en: Should crusaders gather at suitable places at an opportune time to cross the sea with blessing for the assistance of the holy Land?
lyo1-colli-constitution6-en: May conservators defend those entrusted to them from manifest injury and violence, without extending their power to matters requiring judicial investigation?
lyo1-colli-constitution7-en: Do Roman-church legates lack power from the legate's office alone to confer benefices, unless that power is specially granted, without restricting cardinals acting as such?
lyo1-colli-constitution8-en: May a judge delegate order a party to appear in person only with a special apostolic concession, except in a criminal case or when the law requires personal appearance for truth or an oath of calumny?
lyo1-colli-constitution9-en: Does a peremptory exception raised before contestation of the suit fail to prevent contestation, unless it concerns a matter already judged, concluded, or settled?
lyo1-colli-constitution10-en: In civil suits, may a judge refuse to hold up the major issue because of an objection of robbery, except as the constitution allows, so that malicious delays do not ruin ecclesiastical cases?
lyo1-colli-constitution11-en: Must a plaintiff who fails to appear on the date he caused to be cited pay the defendant's expenses and give surety before being admitted to another citation?
lyo1-colli-constitution12-en: May a person suing a possessor for a dignity, parsonage, or benefice not be admitted to possession for preservation merely because of the other's contumacy?
lyo1-colli-constitution13-en: May judges accept negative assertions that can be proved only by the opponent's admission when equity makes that expedient?
lyo1-colli-constitution14-en: Does the exception of major excommunication hold up a suit and delay the agents whenever it is produced in the proceedings?
lyo1-colli-constitution15-en: Must ecclesiastical judges keep dislike, undue favor, fear, and hope of reward from overturning justice in their judgments?
lyo1-colli-constitution16-en: If someone appeals because of an interlocutory decree or grievance, must the reason be put in writing at once and a writ obtained stating why the appeal was or was not granted?
lyo1-colli-constitution17-en: When suspicion is raised against a judge and two arbitrators disagree without summoning a third, must a time be fixed for them to agree or summon a third rather than leave the case stalled by excommunication?
lyo1-colli-constitution18-en: If a prince, prelate, or other person causes a Christian to be killed by assassins, is that wickedness to be struck with ecclesiastical punishment to defend souls and restrain such cruelty?
lyo1-colli-constitution19-en: Must a sentence of excommunication be pronounced in writing with the reason expressly stated, and a copy given to the excommunicated person within a month if requested?
lyo1-colli-constitution20-en: When someone seeks precautionary absolution claiming an excommunication is void, is absolution not to be refused according to the rules the constitution lays down for such cases?
lyo1-colli-constitution21-en: May a judge not pronounce major excommunication, before a canonical warning, on those who associate with persons he has already excommunicated in ways that incur only minor excommunication?
lyo1-colli-constitution22-en: Do bishops and higher prelates avoid automatic interdict or suspension under a decree unless bishops and superiors are expressly mentioned in it?
lyo1-bull-deposition-frederick-ii-en: Is Frederick II denounced as cast out by God from kingdom and empire, deprived of every honor and dignity, with all bound by loyalty to him absolved and forbidden to obey him as emperor or king?
nic1-canon1-en: May one castrated by physicians in sickness or by barbarians remain among the clergy, while one who castrates himself in sound health must cease ministry and not be promoted?
nic1-canon2-en: Must recent converts from heathenism not be advanced straightway after baptism to the episcopate or the presbyterate, but given longer trial?
nic1-canon3-en: Is any bishop, presbyter, deacon, or cleric forbidden to have a subintroducta dwelling with him, except a mother, sister, aunt, or other person beyond all suspicion?
nic1-canon4-en: Should a bishop be appointed by all the bishops of the province, or at least by three with the absent bishops' written consent, with ratification left to the Metropolitan?
nic1-canon5-en: Must those excommunicated in one province not be readmitted by others, with provincial synods held twice a year to examine whether the excommunication was captious or contentious?
nic1-canon6-en: Do the ancient customs stand that the Bishop of Alexandria has jurisdiction in Egypt, Libya, and Pentapolis, as Rome also has its custom, and likewise Antioch and other provinces their privileges, so that no one made bishop without the Metropolitan's consent is a bishop?
nic1-canon7-en: Should the Bishop of Aelia (Jerusalem), saving the Metropolis's due dignity, have the next place of honor by custom and ancient tradition?
nic1-canon8-en: May ordained Cathari who come over to the Catholic and Apostolic Church remain in the clergy if they profess in writing to follow Catholic dogmas, including communion with the twice-married and with penitents who lapsed in persecution?
nic1-canon9-en: Does the Church refuse to admit as clergy those advanced without examination, or who confessed crime yet had hands laid on them in violation of the canon, since only the blameless is required?
nic1-canon10-en: If any who have lapsed were ordained through ignorance or even with the ordainers' knowledge, must they be deposed when discovered, without prejudice to the Church's canon?
nic1-canon11-en: Are those who fell without compulsion in Licinius's tyranny, though undeserving of clemency, to pass three years as hearers, seven as prostrators, and two communicating in prayers without the oblation, if they heartily repent?
nic1-canon12-en: Must those who cast aside military girdles and later regained military stations by gifts pass three years as hearers and ten as prostrators, with the character of their repentance carefully examined?
nic1-canon13-en: Must a person at the point of death not be deprived of the last Viaticum, and if restored after receiving communion in despair of life, remain among those who communicate in prayers only?
nic1-canon14-en: After lapsed catechumens have passed three years only as hearers, shall they pray with the catechumens?
nic1-canon15-en: Is it forbidden for bishop, presbyter, or deacon to pass from city to city, so that any such attempt after this decree is utterly void and he is restored to the Church for which he was ordained?
nic1-canon16-en: Must clergy who recklessly leave their own church not be received by another, but be restored to their parishes or else excommunicated, and is ordination of another's enrolled cleric without his bishop's consent void?
nic1-canon17-en: If any of the clergy is found receiving usury after this decree, whether by secret transaction or other contrivance, shall he be deposed and his name stricken from the list?
nic1-canon18-en: Must deacons remain within their bounds as ministers of the bishop and inferiors of the presbyters, not administer the Eucharist to those who offer, nor touch it before the bishops, but receive after the presbyters?
nic1-canon19-en: Must Paulianists who flee to the Catholic Church be rebaptized, and if any among their former clergy are found blameless and suitable, be rebaptized and then ordained by a Catholic bishop?
nic1-canon20-en: Should prayer be made to God standing on the Lord's Day and in the days of Pentecost, rather than kneeling, so that this is uniformly observed everywhere?
nic1-synodal-letter-en: Did the bishops assembled at Nicaea communicate to the Church of Alexandria and the orthodox in Egypt, Pentapolis, and Libya the matters concerning the faith that the synod had considered?
lat1-canon1-en: Is anyone ordained or promoted in the Church for money to be utterly deprived of the office so acquired?
lat1-canon2-en: May those excommunicated by their own bishops not be received into communion by other bishops, abbots, and clergy?
lat1-canon3-en: May no one consecrate as bishop someone not canonically elected, and if anyone does, are both consecrator and consecrated deposed beyond hope of restoration?
lat1-canon4-en: May no archdeacon, archpriest, provost, or dean grant the care of souls or prebends without the bishop's decision or consent, since those matters remain in the bishop's power?
lat1-canon5-en: Are the ordinations made by the heresiarch Burdinus after his condemnation by the Roman church, and those by pseudo-bishops he ordained, null and void?
lat1-canon6-en: May only a priest be ordained to the office of provost, archpriest, or dean, and only a deacon to the office of archdeacon?
lat1-canon7-en: Are priests, deacons, and subdeacons forbidden to live with concubines and wives, or to cohabit with other women except those Nicaea permitted, such as a mother, sister, or aunt beyond suspicion?
lat1-canon8-en: Do lay persons, however religious, have no power to dispose of ecclesiastical business, so that a prince or lay person who arrogates disposition of church things is regarded as sacrilegious?
lat1-canon9-en: Are unions between blood relatives prohibited by divine and secular law, and are those who enter them marked with infamy?
lat1-canon10-en: Do those who set out for Jerusalem to defend the Christian people and overcome the infidels receive remission of sins, with their houses, families, and goods under the protection of blessed Peter and the Roman church?
lat1-canon11-en: Is the immoral practice of dispersing the goods of Porticani who die without heirs against their wishes abolished, so long as the Porticani remain obedient and faithful to the Roman church?
lat1-canon12-en: Are the laity forbidden under anathema to remove offerings from the altars of blessed Peter, the Saviour, St Mary Rotunda, St Nicholas of Bari, St Giles, and other churches, and to fortify or seize churches?
lat1-canon13-en: Is whoever knowingly makes or intentionally spends counterfeit money separated from the communion of the faithful as accursed?
lat1-canon14-en: If anyone attacks pilgrims to Rome or foreigners visiting the shrines, robs them, or troubles merchants with new tolls and fees, is he deprived of Christian communion until he makes reparation?
lat1-canon15-en: Are the determinations of previous Roman pontiffs concerning the peace and truce of God, arson, and the public highways confirmed, so that a violator of a truce who scorns threefold admonition incurs anathema?
lat1-canon16-en: Must monks be subject to their own bishops with humility and obedience, abstain from celebrating masses in public and from visitations of the sick, anointings, and hearing confessions, and have only priests ordained by their bishop for the care of souls?
lat1-canon17-en: Is any military person forbidden under anathema to seize or hold Benevento, the city of blessed Peter, by force?
lat1-canon18-en: Must priests for parish churches be appointed by the bishops, to whom they answer for the care of souls, and may they not receive tithes or churches from lay persons without the bishops' consent?
lat1-canon19-en: Is the service monasteries and their churches have paid from Gregory VII until now allowed, while abbots and monks are altogether forbidden to hold possessions of churches and bishops by a thirty years' provision?
lat1-canon20-en: Are churches and what belongs to them—clerics, monks, lay brothers, those who come to pray, and what they bring—under protection, so that one who harms them and does not amend within thirty days is banished and smitten with anathema?
lat1-canon21-en: Are priests, deacons, subdeacons, and monks absolutely forbidden to have concubines or contract marriages, and are such marriage contracts void?
lat1-canon22-en: Are alienations of the property of the exarchate of Ravenna, especially those by Otto, Jeremias, and perhaps Philip, condemned, and are alienations and simoniacal ordinations by intruded or irregularly elected bishops or abbots without the clergy's consent invalid?
df-ch1-canon1-en: Is there one true God, creator and lord of things visible and invisible?
df-ch2-canon1-en: Can the one, true God, our creator and lord, be known with certainty from the things that have been made, by the natural light of human reason?
df-ch3-canon1-en: Is human reason so independent that faith cannot be commanded by God?
df-ch4-canon1-en: Does divine revelation contain true mysteries properly so-called that cannot all be understood and demonstrated by properly trained reason from natural principles alone?
df-ch1-canon2-en: Does there exist nothing besides matter?
df-ch2-canon2-en: Is it possible, and expedient, that human beings should be taught by means of divine revelation about God and the worship that should be shown him?
df-ch3-canon2-en: Is divine faith distinct from natural knowledge about God and moral matters, so that revealed truth must be believed because of the authority of God who reveals it?
df-ch4-canon2-en: May the assertions of human studies be maintained as true even when opposed to divine revelation, and may they not be forbidden by the church?
df-ch1-canon3-en: Is the substance or essence of God one and the same as that of all things?
df-ch2-canon3-en: Can a human being be divinely elevated to a knowledge and perfection which exceeds the natural, or must he of himself finally possess all truth and goodness by continual development alone?
df-ch3-canon3-en: Can divine revelation be made credible by external signs, or ought people to be moved to faith only by each one's internal experience or private inspiration?
df-ch4-canon3-en: Given the advancement of knowledge, may a sense different from that which the church has understood and understands be assigned to the dogmas she has propounded?
df-ch1-canon4-en: Did finite things emanate from the divine substance, or does the divine essence by evolution become all things, or is God an indefinite being that by self-determination establishes all things?
df-ch2-canon4-en: Must the complete books of sacred scripture with all their parts, as listed by the council of Trent, be received as sacred and canonical and as divinely inspired?
df-ch3-canon4-en: Are miracles possible and knowable with certainty, including those in sacred scripture, so that the divine origin of the Christian religion can be proved from them?
df-ch1-canon5-en: Were the world and all things in it, spiritual and material, produced according to their whole substance out of nothing by God, by his free will, for the glory of God?
df-ch3-canon5-en: Is the assent of Christian faith free rather than necessarily produced by arguments of human reason, and is God's grace necessary for more than living faith which works by charity?
df-ch3-canon6-en: Is the condition of the faithful and of those who have not yet attained the true faith alike, so that Catholics may justly suspend assent until they complete a scientific demonstration of their faith?
df-ch1-p1-en: Is there one true and living God, creator and lord of heaven and earth, almighty, eternal, immeasurable, incomprehensible, and infinite in will, understanding, and every perfection?
df-ch2-p1-en: Can God, the source and end of all things, be known with certainty from created things by the natural power of human reason?
df-ch3-p1-en: Are we obliged to yield to God the revealer full submission of intellect and will by faith?
df-ch4-p1-en: Is there a twofold order of knowledge, distinct both as regards its source and as regards its object?
df-ch1-p2-en: Is God one, singular, completely simple and unchangeable spiritual substance, in reality and essence distinct from the world and supremely happy in himself?
df-ch2-p2-en: Has God revealed himself and the eternal laws of his will to the human race by a supernatural way, speaking of old by the prophets and in these last days by a Son?
df-ch3-p2-en: Is faith a supernatural virtue by which, with God's grace, we believe what he has revealed because of his authority who can neither deceive nor be deceived, not because reason perceives its intrinsic truth?
df-ch4-p2-en: Do we know at one level by natural reason and at the other level by divine faith?
df-ch1-p3-en: Did the one true God, by an absolutely free plan, bring into being from nothing the spiritual and bodily created order, and thereafter the human composed of spirit and body?
df-ch2-p3-en: Thanks to divine revelation, can matters concerning God that are not beyond human reason be known by everyone without difficulty, with firm certitude and without error?
df-ch3-p3-en: Is faith the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen?
df-ch4-p3-en: Besides what natural reason can attain, are there mysteries hidden in God that are incapable of being known unless they are divinely revealed?
df-ch1-p4-en: Does God protect and govern everything he has brought into being by his providence, which orders all things and sees even what free creatures will bring about?
df-ch2-p4-en: Is revelation absolutely necessary because God directed human beings to a supernatural end that utterly surpasses the understanding of the human mind?
df-ch3-p4-en: Did God will that external indications of revelation—especially miracles and prophecies—be linked to the Spirit's internal assistance so that the submission of faith accords with reason?
df-ch4-p4-en: Can reason achieve some profitable understanding of the mysteries by analogy and connection, yet never penetrate them as it does truths that form its proper object?
df-ch2-p5-en: Is supernatural revelation contained in written books and unwritten traditions received from Christ or by the Holy Spirit's dictation and passed down to us?
df-ch3-p5-en: Did Moses, the prophets, Christ our Lord, and the apostles work clear miracles and deliver prophecies that confirm the divine message?
df-ch4-p5-en: Even though faith is above reason, can there ever be any real disagreement between faith and reason, since the same God reveals mysteries and endows the mind with reason?
df-ch2-p6-en: Are the complete books of the old and new Testament with all their parts, as listed by Trent and found in the old Latin Vulgate, to be received as sacred and canonical?
df-ch3-p6-en: Is the inspiration and illumination of the Holy Spirit necessary to accept the gospel preaching as required for salvation, even though the assent of faith is not a blind movement of the mind?
df-ch4-p6-en: Can God deny himself, or can truth ever be in opposition to truth?
df-ch2-p7-en: Does the church hold the biblical books sacred and canonical because, written under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, they have God as their author and were committed to the church?
df-ch3-p7-en: Is faith in itself, even though it may not work through charity, a gift of God whose operation belongs to the order of salvation as true obedience to God?
df-ch4-p7-en: Is every assertion contrary to the truth of enlightened faith totally false?
df-ch2-p8-en: In matters of faith and morals, must that meaning of holy scripture be held true which holy mother church held and holds, since it is her right to judge its true sense?
df-ch3-p8-en: Are all those things to be believed by divine and catholic faith which are contained in scripture and tradition and proposed by the church as divinely revealed, by solemn judgment or ordinary and universal magisterium?
df-ch4-p8-en: Has the church, charged with preserving the deposit of faith, the right and duty of condemning what wrongly passes for knowledge, lest anyone be led astray by philosophy and empty deceit?
df-ch2-p9-en: Is it permissible for anyone to interpret holy scripture in a sense contrary to the church's judgment or against the unanimous consent of the fathers?
df-ch3-p9-en: Can anyone achieve justification without faith, or attain eternal life unless he or she perseveres in faith to the end?
df-ch4-p9-en: Are faithful Christians forbidden to defend as legitimate conclusions of science opinions known to be contrary to the doctrine of faith, especially if condemned by the church?
df-ch3-p10-en: Did God, through his only-begotten Son, found the church and endow her with clear notes so that she might be recognised as the guardian and teacher of the revealed word?
df-ch4-p10-en: Can faith and reason never be at odds, but rather mutually support each other, as right reason establishes faith's foundations and faith protects reason from errors?
df-ch3-p11-en: Do all those many and marvellous things divinely ordained to make for the manifest credibility of the Christian faith belong to the catholic church alone?
df-ch4-p11-en: Does the church assist and promote the development of human arts and studies in many ways, acknowledging that their advantages flow from God, the lord of sciences?
df-ch3-p12-en: Is the church herself, by her propagation, holiness, fertility in goodness, catholic unity, and unconquerable stability, a great and perpetual motive of credibility and evidence of her divine mission?
df-ch4-p12-en: While admitting just freedom for studies to use their own principles and methods, does the church take care that they not become infected with errors conflicting with divine teaching?
df-ch3-p13-en: Does the church, like a standard lifted up for the nations, invite those who have not yet believed and assure her children that the faith they profess rests on the firmest foundations?
df-ch4-p13-en: Is the doctrine of the faith which God has revealed a divine deposit committed to the spouse of Christ to be faithfully protected and infallibly promulgated, not a philosophical discovery perfected by human intelligence?
df-ch3-p14-en: Does the Lord stir up those who go astray by his grace so they may come to the knowledge of the truth, and confirm those in his light so they may persevere unless they first abandon him?
df-ch4-p14-en: Must that meaning of the sacred dogmas which holy mother church has once declared always be maintained, without abandonment under pretext of a more profound understanding?
df-ch3-p15-en: Is the situation of those who by faith have embraced the catholic truth unlike that of those who follow a false religion, so that they can never have just cause for changing or calling that faith into question?
df-ch4-p15-en: May understanding, knowledge, and wisdom increase in the church only in the same doctrine, the same sense, and the same understanding?
df-ch3-p16-en: Should we, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith, hold the unshakeable confession of our hope and not neglect so great a salvation?
df-closing-en: Must all faithful Christians, especially those in authority or who teach, contribute zeal to eliminate these errors from the church and spread the light of the pure faith?
df-preamble-en: Did the Son of God, redeemer of the human race, promise to be with his church militant upon earth all days even to the end of the world, assisting her when she teaches?
pa-ch1-canon1-en: Was blessed Peter appointed by Christ as prince of all the apostles and visible head of the whole church militant, receiving a true primacy of jurisdiction and not of honour only?
pa-ch3-canon1-en: Does the Roman pontiff have full and supreme power of jurisdiction over the whole church in faith, morals, discipline, and government, ordinary and immediate over all churches and pastors?
pa-ch4-canon1-en: Must the defined dogma of the Roman pontiff's infallible teaching authority be accepted?
pa-ch1-p1-en: Was a primacy of jurisdiction over the whole church of God immediately and directly promised to the blessed apostle Peter and conferred on him by Christ the Lord?
pa-ch2-p1-en: Must that which Christ established in blessed Peter for the continual salvation and permanent benefit of the church remain for ever in the church founded upon a rock?
pa-ch3-p1-en: Do the apostolic see and the Roman pontiff hold a world-wide primacy, the Roman pontiff being successor of blessed Peter, true vicar of Christ, head of the whole church and father and teacher of all Christians?
pa-ch4-p1-en: Does the apostolic primacy which the Roman pontiff possesses as successor of Peter include also the supreme power of teaching?
pa-ch1-p2-en: Did the Lord say to Simon alone, after his confession, "You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church," promising him the keys of the kingdom of heaven?
pa-ch2-p2-en: Does blessed Peter, who received the keys of the kingdom from Christ, live and preside and exercise judgment to this day in his successors the bishops of the holy Roman see?
pa-ch3-p2-en: By divine ordinance, does the Roman church possess a pre-eminence of ordinary power over every other church, and is the Roman pontiff's jurisdictional power episcopal and immediate over clergy and faithful?
pa-ch4-p2-en: As the fathers of Constantinople IV professed, has the catholic religion always been preserved unblemished in the apostolic see, confirming "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church"?
pa-ch1-p3-en: Was it to Peter alone that Jesus after his resurrection confided the jurisdiction of supreme pastor and ruler of his whole fold, saying "Feed my lambs, feed my sheep"?
pa-ch2-p3-en: Does whoever succeeds to the chair of Peter obtain by Christ's institution the primacy of Peter over the whole church?
pa-ch3-p3-en: By unity with the Roman pontiff in communion and in profession of the same faith, does the church of Christ become one flock under one supreme shepherd?
pa-ch4-p3-en: Did the Roman pontiffs' predecessors strive that the saving teaching of Christ be spread among all peoples and kept pure and uncontaminated wherever received?
pa-ch1-p4-en: Did Christ endow Peter, in preference to the rest of the apostles taken singly or collectively, with a true and proper primacy of jurisdiction?
pa-ch2-p4-en: Has it always been necessary for every church—the faithful throughout the world—to be in agreement with the Roman church because of its more effective leadership?
pa-ch3-p4-en: Is this teaching of the catholic truth about the Roman pontiff's primacy such that no one can depart from it without endangering his faith and salvation?
pa-ch4-p4-en: Have bishops of the whole world, individually or in synods, referred dangers concerning the faith to this apostolic see, so that damage to the faith be repaired where the faith can know no failing?
pa-ch1-p5-en: Was this primacy conferred immediately and directly on blessed Peter himself, rather than on the church so as to be transmitted to him only as her minister?
pa-ch3-p5-en: Does the supreme pontiff's power assert, support, and defend the ordinary and immediate episcopal jurisdiction by which bishops tend and govern their particular flocks?
pa-ch4-p5-en: Have the Roman pontiffs, by councils, consultation of the churches, synods, or other means, defined as doctrines to be held those things they knew to keep with sacred scripture and apostolic tradition?
pa-ch3-p6-en: Does the Roman pontiff have the right, in governing the whole church, to communicate freely with the pastors and flocks of the entire church so they may be taught and guided by him?
pa-ch4-p6-en: Was the Holy Spirit promised to Peter's successors so that they might religiously guard and faithfully expound the deposit of faith, not so that they might make known some new doctrine by revelation?
pa-ch3-p7-en: May communication of the supreme head with pastors and flocks be lawfully obstructed, or made to depend on civil confirmation before apostolic determinations have force?
pa-ch4-p7-en: Was the gift of truth and never-failing faith divinely conferred on Peter and his successors so that the whole flock might be kept from error, nourished with heavenly doctrine, and preserved in unity?
pa-ch3-p8-en: Is the Roman pontiff the supreme judge of the faithful, so that recourse may be had to his judgment in ecclesiastical cases and the sentence of the apostolic see is not subject to revision by anyone?
pa-ch4-p8-en: Is it necessary to affirm solemnly the prerogative which the only-begotten Son of God was pleased to attach to the supreme pastoral office?
pa-preamble-en: Did the eternal shepherd determine to build a church in which all the faithful are linked by one faith and charity, praying also for those who would believe through the apostles' word?
con4-canon1-en: Must the declarations and teachings of the holy fathers be kept as lamps always alight, esteemed like a second word of God illuminating the road of divine justice?
con4-canon2-en: Must everything promulgated by Popes Nicholas and Hadrian in synod for the defence of the church of Constantinople and patriarch Ignatius, and for the condemnation of Photius, be maintained and observed?
con4-canon3-en: Should the sacred image of our Lord Jesus Christ be venerated with honour equal to that given to the book of the holy gospels and the representation of the precious cross, because of honour to the archetype?
con4-canon4-en: Was Photius never a bishop, must those he consecrated or advanced not remain in that state, and are his sacerdotal acts and renovated altars to be treated as abrogated or reconsecrated?
con4-canon5-en: May nobody who is a neophyte in the faith or priestly office be made a bishop, lest he be puffed up and fall into the judgment and snare of the devil?
con4-canon6-en: Did Photius unlawfully designate false vicars of the eastern patriarchal sees and cobble together lying records, which this synod burned, after Pope Nicholas's just condemnations?
con4-canon7-en: May painting of holy images and teaching of divine and human wisdom not be done by the unworthy, so that whoever admits such persons to paint sacred images or teach is removed from office or punished?
con4-canon8-en: Apart from what custom demands at episcopal consecrations to witness the purity of faith, may nobody demand from priests written guarantees designed for a patriarch's security and permanence?
con4-canon9-en: Is Photius's practice of giving signed documents to followers learning a wisdom alien to the holy fathers forbidden, while competent persons not enslaved to error may teach and study?
con4-canon10-en: May no lay person, monk, or cleric separate himself from communion with his own patriarch before careful enquiry and judgment in synod, and must the same hold toward metropolitans and patriarchs?
con4-canon11-en: Does a man or woman have one rational and intellectual soul, so that those who teach as dogma that a human being has two souls are under anathema?
con4-canon12-en: If any bishop received consecration through the manipulation and constraint of civil authorities, must he be deposed as one who desired God's gift from human machinations rather than from God's will?
con4-canon13-en: May clerics of the great church who served in lower orders rise to higher dignities if worthy, while outsiders and managers of leading persons' estates must not be inducted into that clergy?
con4-canon14-en: Should bishops be held worthy of all honour by rulers and ruled alike, and must they not go far from their churches to meet generals or high officials in a way unfitting their spiritual dignity?
con4-canon15-en: May a bishop sell or dispose of precious objects or consecrated vessels only for the redemption of captives as the ancient canons allow, and not hand over church endowments by emphyteutic leases to the church's damage?
con4-canon16-en: Is it forbidden for laymen to adopt priestly or episcopal dress and ornaments and to mock elections, promotions, and consecrations of bishops as court buffoonery?
con4-canon17-en: Must the ancient custom be preserved so that the prelates of old and new Rome, Antioch, and Jerusalem have authority over the metropolitans they promote or confirm, as Alexandria's custom was ordered at Nicaea?
con4-canon18-en: Must goods or privileges belonging to the churches by long custom or grant, possessed for thirty years, in no way be removed by force of any secular person from the prelate's jurisdiction?
con4-canon19-en: May no archbishop or metropolitan leave his own church to visit other churches under pretext of visitation and abuse his authority by burdening fellow-bishops and suffragans with shameful love of gain?
con4-canon20-en: May people who received lands by emphyteusis not be callously expelled without agreement of those entrusted with such decisions, unless the leaseholder first hears the objections through suitable mediators?
con4-canon21-en: Should no secular powers treat patriarchs with disrespect or seek to move them from their high positions, but esteem them as worthy of all honour and reverence?
con4-canon22-en: Must the promotion and consecration of bishops be done by election and decision of the college of bishops, with no lay authority or ruler intervening in the election of a patriarch, metropolitan, or bishop?
con4-canon23-en: May no bishop unreasonably make a gift of properties belonging to other churches, usurping other bishops' authority, nor may anyone else so transact?
con4-canon24-en: May metropolitans not through negligence commit to subject bishops the divine offices, litanies, and sacred ministries personal to themselves, making those bishops seem like their servants?
con4-canon25-en: Must bishops, priests, deacons, and subdeacons of the great church consecrated by Methodius and Ignatius who support the usurper Photius and reject harmony with this synod be deposed and suspended from sacerdotal functions?
con4-canon26-en: Does a priest or deacon deposed by his bishop, or claiming injustice, have the right to have recourse to the metropolitan of his province to denounce a deposition he thinks unjust?
con4-canon27-en: In ecclesiastical promotions and consecrations, must the marks signifying each person's rank be kept according to traditional usages, so that bishops permitted the pallium wear it only at the proper times and places?
lat4-constitution1-en: Is there only one true God, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost—three Persons but one essence— the Son from the Father only and the Holy Ghost equally from both, consubstantial, coequal, and coeternal?
lat4-constitution2-en: Is there one supreme entity which is truly Father, Son, and Holy Ghost—only a trinity, not a quaternity—so that Joachim's book charging Peter Lombard with quaternity is condemned?
